input_references.role: Timestamped GPS points for the observed courier-day

metadata.goal: Analyze the spatial and temporal patterns of courier delivery activity in the selected delivery area.
metadata.header: Time-Conditioned Courier Path and Order Coverage
metadata.dataset_description: The main table contains 72 delivery orders across three time periods for one courier-day. Receipt and destination coordinates are derived from timestamped points on supporting GPS trajectory fragments in a shared case coordinate frame. The trajectory_segment field identifies each contiguous observed fragment; gaps between fragments are not drawn as movement.

insight_list.insight: During midday, receipt and destination activity is tightly concentrated inside the central service core, unlike the wider evening and late-evening patterns.

plot.title: Courier Paths and Order Locations across Three Time Periods
plot.description: All three maps use the same coordinate extent and show the GPS path, receipt points, destination points, and the shaded central service core.

insight_list.question: How do the GPS path and the spatial distribution of receipt and destination locations differ across midday, evening, and late evening?
insight_list.actionable_insight: Compare the point concentration and route coverage using the same map extent across the three periods.
insight_list.code:
import pandas as pd
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt
d = df.copy(); t = user_df.copy()
d['period'] = d['receipt_time'].str.extract(r'(\d+):')[0].astype(int).map(lambda h: 'midday' if 11 <= h < 15 else ('evening' if 17 <= h < 20 else 'late_evening'))
t['period'] = t['gps_time'].str.extract(r'(\d+):')[0].astype(int).map(lambda h: 'midday' if 11 <= h < 15 else ('evening' if 17 <= h < 20 else 'late_evening'))
fig, axes = plt.subplots(1,3,figsize=(18,6), sharex=True, sharey=True)
for ax, period in zip(axes,['midday','evening','late_evening']):
 q=d[d.period==period]; tr=t[t.period==period]
 for _, s in tr.groupby('trajectory_segment'): ax.plot(s.lng,s.lat,color='gray')
 ax.scatter(q.receipt_lng,q.receipt_lat,marker='s',c='teal'); ax.scatter(q.poi_lng,q.poi_lat,c='darkorange'); ax.set_title(period); ax.set_aspect('equal')
plt.show()

insight_list.insight: During the evening period, both the courier path and order locations cover a wider part of the central service area than at midday.

insight_value.comparison: evening spatial coverage exceeds midday while remaining within the central service core

import pandas as pd
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt
d=df.copy(); t=user_df.copy()
d['period']=d['receipt_time'].str.extract(r'(\d+):')[0].astype(int).map(lambda h:'midday' if 11<=h<15 else ('evening' if 17<=h<20 else 'late_evening'))
t['period']=t['gps_time'].str.extract(r'(\d+):')[0].astype(int).map(lambda h:'midday' if 11<=h<15 else ('evening' if 17<=h<20 else 'late_evening'))

for ax,period in zip(axes,['midday','evening']):
 q=d[d.period==period]; tr=t[t.period==period]

insight_list.question: How does the distribution of receipt and destination event dispersion compare across midday, evening, and late evening?
insight_list.actionable_insight: Compare the full event-spread distributions across periods rather than relying on a single late-evening map.
insight_list.code:
import pandas as pd
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt
d=df.copy(); d['period']=d['receipt_time'].str.extract(r'(\d+):')[0].astype(int).map(lambda h:'midday' if 11<=h<15 else ('evening' if 17<=h<20 else 'late_evening'))
events=pd.concat([d[['period','receipt_lng','receipt_lat']].rename(columns={'receipt_lng':'lng','receipt_lat':'lat'}),d[['period','poi_lng','poi_lat']].rename(columns={'poi_lng':'lng','poi_lat':'lat'})])
centres=events.groupby('period')[['lng','lat']].mean(); events=events.join(centres,on='period',rsuffix='_centre'); events['distance_km']=((events.lng-events.lng_centre)**2+(events.lat-events.lat_centre)**2)**.5/1000
for period,g in events.groupby('period'): plt.scatter(g.distance_km,[period]*len(g),alpha=.55,label=period)
plt.xlabel('distance from period centroid (km)'); plt.legend(); plt.show()

insights: During midday, receipt and destination activity is tightly concentrated inside the central service core, unlike the wider evening and late-evening patterns.
During the evening period, both the courier path and order locations cover a wider part of the central service area than at midday.
During late evening, receipt and destination locations spread across multiple separated edge clusters rather than a single central cluster.
summary: Across one observed courier-day, midday activity is compact and concentrated in the central service core. Evening activity covers a wider portion of that same central service area. Late-evening activity is distributed across several separated edge clusters. In every view, receipt and destination coordinates are sampled from the GPS path of their corresponding period.
